behaviours.title: An account never used reads as balance 0 with no entries
behaviours.given: a new Ledger where account 'ghost' was never opened or used
behaviours.then: the balance is 0 and the entries list is empty
behaviours.contrary_then: the balance of an unknown account is reported as undefined
contrary_alternatives: reading an unknown account throws an 'unknown account' error
reading the balance silently opens the account

behaviours.title: Opening an existing account again keeps its balance
behaviours.then: the balance stays 100 and the deposit entry remains
behaviours.contrary_then: re-opening resets the account to balance 0
contrary_alternatives: re-opening an existing account throws an 'already open' error

behaviours.title: Deposit of 0 or a negative amount is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: both return { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance of 'a' stays 0 with no entries
behaviours.contrary_then: a deposit of 0 is accepted as a harmless no-op returning ok: true
contrary_alternatives: a negative deposit is treated as a withdrawal of 5
zero deposits are accepted and record a 0 entry

behaviours.title: Repeating a deposit with the same txnId succeeds but credits only once
behaviours.then: the repeat returns { ok: true } and the balance stays 100 with one entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the repeat is credited again and the balance becomes 200
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with a 'duplicate' reason and the balance stays 100

behaviours.title: Deposit amounts are rounded to the nearest cent, half a cent rounding up
behaviours.then: 'a' holds 10.01 (entry amount 10.01) and 'b' holds 10
behaviours.contrary_then: half a cent is dropped, so 'a' holds 10
contrary_alternatives: amounts are stored unrounded so 'a' holds 10.005
amounts with more than two decimals are rejected

behaviours.title: Foreign deposit credits amount times rate as a deposit
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } and 'a' holds 150 with a 'deposit' entry of 150
behaviours.contrary_then: the amount is credited without conversion, so 'a' holds 100
contrary_alternatives: the amount is divided by the rate so 'a' holds 66.67
a conversion fee is taken so 'a' holds less than 150

behaviours.title: Foreign deposit with rate 0 or amount 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: both return { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and 'a' stays at 0
behaviours.contrary_then: a rate of 0 is rejected as 'amount-too-small'
contrary_alternatives: a rate of 0 is accepted and credits 0, returning ok: true
a rate of 0 falls back to a rate of 1 and credits 100

behaviours.title: Foreign deposit worth less than half a cent is rejected as amount-too-small; half a cent becomes 0.01
behaviours.then: the first returns { ok: false, reason: 'amount-too-small' } with 'a' at 0; the second returns { ok: true } with 'b' at 0.01
behaviours.contrary_then: the first is accepted with ok: true and credits nothing
contrary_alternatives: the first is rounded up and credits 0.01
the second is also rejected as amount-too-small

behaviours.title: Foreign deposit with an already used txnId is acknowledged without crediting
behaviours.when: depositForeign('a', 50, 2, 'x1') is made with the same txnId
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } and 'a' stays at 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the foreign deposit is credited and 'a' holds 200
contrary_alternatives: the foreign deposit is rejected with a 'duplicate' reason

behaviours.title: Withdrawal of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and 'a' stays at 100 (no fee taken)
behaviours.contrary_then: the zero withdrawal is accepted and only the minimum fee of 0.50 is charged, leaving 99.5
contrary_alternatives: the zero withdrawal is accepted as a no-op with ok: true

behaviours.title: Repeating a withdrawal with the same txnId succeeds without a second debit
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } and 'a' stays at 899
behaviours.contrary_then: the repeat is debited again, leaving 798
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with a 'duplicate' reason and the balance stays 899

behaviours.title: Withdrawal fee is 1% of the amount and is included in the withdrawal entry
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true }, 'a' holds 899 and the withdrawal entry amount is 101 (100 plus fee 1)
behaviours.contrary_then: no fee is charged and 'a' holds 900
contrary_alternatives: a 2% fee is charged and 'a' holds 898
the fee is recorded as a separate entry and the withdrawal entry shows 100

behaviours.title: Withdrawal fee is at least 0.50
behaviours.then: the fee is 0.50 and 'a' holds 89.5
behaviours.contrary_then: the fee is 1% = 0.10 and 'a' holds 89.9
contrary_alternatives: no fee is charged on small withdrawals and 'a' holds 90
the minimum fee is 1.00 and 'a' holds 89

behaviours.title: Withdrawal fee is capped at 25
behaviours.then: the fee is 25 and 'a' holds 1975
behaviours.contrary_then: the fee is uncapped at 30 and 'a' holds 1970
contrary_alternatives: the cap is 10 and 'a' holds 1990
the withdrawal is refused because it is too large for a single transaction

behaviours.title: Withdrawal fee rounds a part-cent up to the next cent
behaviours.then: the fee is 0.51 and 'a' holds 49.48
behaviours.contrary_then: the fee is rounded to 0.50 and 'a' holds 49.49
contrary_alternatives: the fee is kept unrounded and 'a' holds 49.4899

behaviours.title: Withdrawal must be covered including its fee
behaviours.when: withdraw('a', 99.5, 'w1') (fee 1.00, total 100.50) and withdraw('b', 99, 'w2') (fee 0.99, total 99.99) are made
behaviours.then: the first returns { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and 'a' stays 100; the second succeeds and 'b' holds 0.01
behaviours.contrary_then: the first is accepted because 99.5 alone fits within the balance
contrary_alternatives: the first is accepted with the fee reduced to what remains, leaving 'a' at 0
the second is also refused because some minimum balance must remain

behaviours.title: A withdrawal that takes the balance exactly to 0 is allowed
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } and 'a' holds 0
behaviours.contrary_then: it is refused as insufficient-funds because the balance must stay above 0
contrary_alternatives: it is accepted with no fee and 'a' holds 1

behaviours.title: Withdrawals total at most 5000 per account; the fee does not count toward it
behaviours.then: the first succeeds leaving 14975 (fee 25); the second returns { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and 'a' stays at 14975
behaviours.contrary_then: the second is accepted because there is still room under the limit
contrary_alternatives: the first is already refused because amount plus fee (5025) exceeds 5000
the limit is 10000 and both succeed

behaviours.title: A single withdrawal of 5000.01 is refused as daily-limit
behaviours.given: account 'a' holds 20000 and has not withdrawn anything
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and 'a' stays at 20000
behaviours.contrary_then: it is accepted, leaving 14974.99
contrary_alternatives: it is partially paid out up to 5000

behaviours.title: Insufficient funds is reported before the daily limit
behaviours.when: withdraw('a', 6000, 'w1') is made (over both the balance and the 5000 limit)
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }
behaviours.contrary_then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' }
contrary_alternatives: it returns a combined reason listing both problems
it is accepted and the account goes overdrawn

behaviours.title: A refused withdrawal does not use up the daily limit
behaviours.when: withdraw('a', 5000.01, 'w1') is refused, then withdraw('a', 5000, 'w2') is made
behaviours.then: the second succeeds and 'a' holds 14975
behaviours.contrary_then: the refused attempt counted toward the limit, so the second is refused as daily-limit
contrary_alternatives: the second is refused because the account is locked after a refused withdrawal

behaviours.title: Transfer of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and 'a' stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: it is accepted as a no-op with ok: true
contrary_alternatives: it is rejected because 'b' does not exist

behaviours.title: Transfer can move the whole balance with no fee; one cent more is refused
behaviours.then: the first succeeds: 'a' holds 0 and 'b' holds 50, with transfer-out and transfer-in entries of 50; the second returns { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }, 'c' stays 50 and 'd' stays 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the second is accepted and 'c' goes to -0.01
contrary_alternatives: transfers carry the withdrawal fee so the first is refused
the first is refused because the balance may not reach 0

behaviours.title: Repeating a transfer with the same txnId succeeds without moving money again
behaviours.given: 'a' held 100 and transfer('a', 'b', 30, 't1') left 'a' at 70 and 'b' at 30
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true }; 'a' stays 70 and 'b' stays 30
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is applied again: 'a' 40 and 'b' 60
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with a 'duplicate' reason

behaviours.title: Split of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount, even with no recipients
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }
behaviours.contrary_then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'no-recipients' }
contrary_alternatives: it is accepted as a no-op

behaviours.title: Split with no recipients is rejected, even when its txnId was already used
behaviours.given: account 'a' holds 100 from a deposit with txnId 'x1'
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'no-recipients' } and 'a' stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: it returns { ok: true } as an already-seen transaction
contrary_alternatives: it is accepted and the 10 simply stays with 'a'

behaviours.title: Repeating a split with the same txnId succeeds without paying again
behaviours.given: 'a' held 100 and split('a', ['b','c'], 10, 's1') left 'a' at 90, 'b' at 5 and 'c' at 5
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true }; 'a' stays 90 and 'b' stays 5
behaviours.contrary_then: the split is paid again: 'a' 80 and 'b' 10
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with a 'duplicate' reason

behaviours.title: Split larger than the payer's balance is refused
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }; 'a' stays 10 and 'b' stays 0
behaviours.contrary_then: it is accepted and 'a' goes to -0.01
contrary_alternatives: only the available 10 is split between the recipients

behaviours.title: Split hands leftover cents one each to the first-listed recipients
behaviours.then: 'a' holds 0 with a 'split-out' entry of 10; 'b' gets 3.34, 'c' 3.33 and 'd' 3.33, each as a 'split-in' entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the leftover cent goes to the last recipient: 'b' 3.33, 'c' 3.33, 'd' 3.34
contrary_alternatives: the leftover cent stays with the payer: each gets 3.33 and 'a' keeps 0.01
the split is refused because 10 does not divide evenly by 3

behaviours.title: Interest uses a 365-day year: 10% for 365 days on 1000 gives 100
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } and 'a' holds 1100 with an 'interest' entry of 100
behaviours.contrary_then: a 360-day year is used, giving 101.38 and a balance of 1101.38
contrary_alternatives: interest compounds daily, giving about 105.16

behaviours.title: Interest is rounded down to the cent
behaviours.then: 'a' is credited 4.10 and holds 1004.1
behaviours.contrary_then: interest is rounded to the nearest cent, 4.11, and 'a' holds 1004.11
contrary_alternatives: interest is computed on a 360-day year giving 4.16

behaviours.title: Interest with rate 0 or 0 days is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: both return { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and 'a' stays 1000
behaviours.contrary_then: both return { ok: true } and credit nothing
contrary_alternatives: a rate of 0 is accepted and records a 0 interest entry

behaviours.title: Repeating an interest posting with the same txnId does not credit again
behaviours.given: 'a' held 1000 and applyInterest('a', 10, 365, 'i1') brought it to 1100
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } and 'a' stays 1100
behaviours.contrary_then: interest is credited again on 1100, bringing 'a' to 1210
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with a 'duplicate' reason

behaviours.title: Interest that comes to 0 returns ok, records nothing, and leaves the txnId reusable
behaviours.when: applyInterest('a', 10, 365, 'i1') is made, then 1000 is deposited as 'd1' and applyInterest('a', 10, 365, 'i1') is made again
behaviours.then: the first returns { ok: true } with no entry; the second, with the same txnId, credits 100 so 'a' holds 1100
behaviours.contrary_then: the first call uses up txnId 'i1', so the second is ignored and 'a' holds 1000
contrary_alternatives: the first call is refused as 'amount-too-small'
the first call records a 0 interest entry
